item.title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystems in Emerging Economies
item.content:encoded:
Ioana Stefan, Mälardalen University

Ikenna Uzuegbunam, Howard University

Brett Anitra Gilbert, American University

Wim Vanhaverbeke, Antwerp University

Kadigia Faccin, Fundação Dom Cabral

Yanbo Wang, University of Hong Kong

Entrepreneurial ecosystems are essential for economic growth, yet research has predominantly focused on developed economies and urban contexts. This special issue seeks to address the underrepresentation of emerging economy research by examining entrepreneurial ecosystems across Africa, Asia, South America, and other developing regions. The issue recognizes that emerging economies face distinct challenges including weak institutions, high uncertainty, limited market sizes, and infrastructure gaps that fundamentally shape how ecosystems develop and function differently than in advanced economies.

The special issue invites research that balances Global North and Global South perspectives, examines ecosystem temporality and evolution, applies systems thinking to understand broader societal impacts, considers multi-level interactions from individual to macro levels, and explores how digitalization uniquely affects emerging economy contexts. Contributors are encouraged to investigate governmental initiatives like Startup Chile and Startup India and to address how entrepreneurial ecosystems can support sustainable development and circular economy practices in developing regions.

Appel publié par Strategic Entrepreneurship Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How entrepreneurial ecosystems emerge, develop and evolve over time in emerging economies compared to advanced economies
  • The role of local and national culture in shaping entrepreneurial ecosystems across different contexts
  • How entrepreneurial ecosystems support refugees, diasporan and returnee entrepreneurs
  • The role of local and international venture funding instruments in emerging economies' entrepreneurial ecosystems
  • Lifecycles and temporal structures of entrepreneurial ecosystems in emerging economies
  • Historical perspectives on entrepreneurial ecosystems and the impact of historical events on their emergence
  • Systems approaches to entrepreneurial ecosystems and their co-evolution with other structures
  • How entrepreneurial ecosystems impact society beyond economic benefits
  • Building blocks of sustainable and resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems
  • Policy effectiveness in supporting entrepreneurial ecosystems in emerging economies
  • Multi-level analysis of interactions between individual, organizational and ecosystem levels
  • Institutional distrust, corruption and their influence on ecosystem orchestration
  • How digitalization and digital technologies shape emergent forms of ecosystems in emerging economies
  • Digital technologies and infrastructures transforming the geography of entrepreneurship in emerging economies

Timeline

  • April 30, 2027: Submission deadline

Associate editors

  • David Sirmon, University of Washington

item.title: Mobilizing, Organizing, and Exploiting Entrepreneurial Judgment Within Ecosystems
item.content:encoded:
David B. Audretsch, Indiana University Bloomington

Maksim Belitski, University of Reading

Rosa Caiazza, Parthenope University of Naples

Nicolai J. Foss, Copenhagen Business School

Donald Siegel, Arizona State University

This special issue examines how entrepreneurial judgment operates within ecosystems involving multiple stakeholders rather than individual entrepreneurs or single firms. While entrepreneurial judgment under uncertainty has traditionally been studied at the individual or firm level, modern entrepreneurship increasingly unfolds through collaborations, alliances, and digital ecosystems where judgment must be communicated, coordinated, and governed among various actors. The issue seeks to advance understanding of ecosystem governance mechanisms and how judgment is mobilized and exploited to support cooperation, competition, and innovation.

Appel publié par Strategic Entrepreneurship Journal. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Communicating tacit judgment in ecosystems
  • Governance and orchestration mechanisms in entrepreneurial ecosystems
  • Partial communicability and protection of entrepreneurial knowledge
  • Distributed judgment and performance across multiple stakeholders
  • Ecosystem dynamics, maturity and role structure
  • AI and decision-support tools in entrepreneurial ecosystems

Timeline

  • March 1, 2027: Deadline for full paper submissions

Associate editors

  • Peter Klein, Baylor University

item.title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Leadership: Processes, Practices, and Contexts
item.content:encoded:
Bruno Fischer, University of Campinas

Aki Harima, Tallinn University of Technology

Sophia Behr, University of Stuttgart

Philip T. Roundy, University of Tennessee Chattanooga

Erik Stam, Utrecht University

Maribel Guerrero, Arizona State University

This special issue examines leadership within entrepreneurial ecosystems as a central yet underexplored phenomenon shaping ecosystem dynamics and outcomes. Rather than treating leadership as a residual category of individual actors or positions, the issue conceptualizes it as a relational process through which direction develops, priorities are negotiated, support is mobilized, and ecosystem development is influenced. The focus spans stable, transforming, and crisis-affected ecosystems, recognizing that contexts such as digitalization, sustainability transitions, and geopolitical disruptions shape how leadership emerges and evolves.

The special issue seeks to move beyond describing static ecosystem structures toward explaining how collective action is generated, coordinated, and sustained over time. It welcomes diverse theoretical perspectives and methodological approaches that develop, challenge, extend, or offer alternative conceptualizations of EE leadership. Research should address who assumes leadership roles, how legitimacy and followership emerge, and how different leadership configurations can compensate for weaknesses in networks, resources, or institutions.

Appel publié par Entrepreneurship & Regional Development. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Conceptualization and theory of entrepreneurial ecosystem (EE) leadership across formal, informal, individual, collective, organizational, distributed, relational, and processual perspectives
  • Dimensions and manifestations of EE leadership (e.g., public, entrepreneurial, community)
  • Interaction between EE leadership and other ecosystem elements such as networks, institutions, finance, or culture
  • Contextual uniqueness shaping forms and theorization of EE leadership across different institutional, cultural, and geographical settings
  • Elements of EE leadership affecting how entrepreneurs and supportive agents cohere around shared norms, values, and goals
  • Relational characteristics (e.g., coordination, collaboration, communication) supporting effective ecosystem leadership
  • Participation, legitimacy, and authority emergence in EE leadership processes
  • How characteristics of ecosystem actors (lived experience, place attachment, prosocial orientation, identity) shape participation in ecosystem leadership
  • Activities, practices, and processes constituting ecosystem leadership and their collective goals
  • Distribution of leadership activities across ecosystem actors and how interactions shape collective direction and coordinated action
  • Forms of leadership and agency emergence, evolution, and enabling coordinated action within EEs
  • Evolution of ecosystem leadership across phases of development and consequences of different forms
  • Conditions under which leadership can compensate for weaknesses in other ecosystem elements
  • Differences in EE leadership across unstable, transforming, and crisis-affected contexts
  • Direction provision under sustainability pressures, digital transformation, geopolitical tension, or resource disruption
  • Negotiation of competing priorities through EE leadership during simultaneous disruptions
  • Measurement and integration of EE leadership activities, practices, and relational processes into existing ecosystem measurement frameworks
  • Use of network metrics to assess distribution of participation, influence, and coordination within EE leadership processes
  • Measures capturing whether EE leadership is concentrated or distributed, formal or informal, and how these configurations change over time

  • February 11, 2027: Paper development workshop within the conference Entrepreneurial Ecosystems in Times of Rapid Transformation in Tallinn, Estonia

item.title: 2SLGBTQIA+ Entrepreneurship: Advancing Theory, Method, and Practice on Identity, Institutions, and Inclusion
item.content:encoded:
Shawna Chen, Brock University

Michael Lounsbury, University of Alberta

Chris Zhang, University of Houston Downtown

While entrepreneurship research has increasingly recognized identity as central to entrepreneurial processes, 2SLGBTQIA+ entrepreneurs remain significantly underexplored in the core literature, particularly regarding how sexuality and gender identity interact with entrepreneurial ecosystems and institutional structures. This special issue aims to advance conceptual, empirical, and methodological understanding of 2SLGBTQIA+ entrepreneurship by examining how these entrepreneurs navigate visibility, stigma, belonging, and legitimacy within broader institutional and spatial contexts.

The special issue welcomes diverse theoretical and methodological approaches, including identity theory, queer-feminist perspectives, intersectionality, institutional theory, and institutional logics. Submissions may employ qualitative, quantitative, or mixed methodologies and are encouraged to bridge theory and practice by including diverse scholarly teams with practitioners involved in entrepreneurship.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business & Entrepreneurship. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • LGBTQ+ identity and entrepreneurial identity work
  • Coming out, concealment, and impression management in venture contexts
  • Intersectionality (e.g., race, gender, class, disability) and layered entrepreneurial experiences
  • Institutional barriers to legitimacy, funding, and recognition
  • Emancipatory entrepreneurship: removing structural constraints through business creation
  • Entrepreneurial ecosystems and their (in)capacity to support LGBTQ+ inclusion
  • Policy and programmatic responses to LGBTQ+ small business development
  • Entrepreneurial wellbeing, belonging, and non-economic goals
  • Comparative studies of LGBTQ+ entrepreneurship across national and regional contexts
  • Methodological approaches for studying LGBTQ+ and equity-deserving entrepreneurs

item.title: Small Business and Entrepreneurship in Sparse Ecosystems: Immigrant Ventures, Innovation and Resilience in Peripheries
item.content:encoded:
Nafisa Yeasmin, University of Oulu

Anisur Faroque, University of Vaasa

Mohammad Osman Gani, University Canada West

Waliul Hasanat, University of Lapland

Hiran Roy, Canadian University

Arctic and remote peripheral regions face demographic decline and labour shortages alongside emerging economic opportunities. Immigrant entrepreneurs play a vital role in sustaining these communities through ventures in tourism, food, logistics, and digital services, yet this phenomenon remains understudied in mainstream entrepreneurship research focused on metropolitan areas.

This special issue examines how immigrant entrepreneurs develop ventures in sparse, geographically isolated, and institutionally thin environments where they navigate regulatory complexity and fragmented support systems. The issue integrates perspectives from entrepreneurship, migration studies, regional development, and sustainability to generate new theoretical insights into entrepreneurial ecosystems in peripheral and extreme contexts.

The special issue welcomes empirical, conceptual, comparative, and policy-oriented contributions exploring how immigrant enterprises mobilize resources, adapt to uncertainty, and shape Arctic and global peripheries. It seeks to expand understanding of entrepreneurial opportunity creation, resilience strategies, and the role of digitalization in these distinctive contexts.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business & Entrepreneurship. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystems & Digital Transformation
item.content:encoded:
Christina Theodoraki, IAE Aix-Marseille Université

Lynda Saoudi, Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1

Mathilde Aubry, EM Normandie

Jean-Michel Sahut, IDRAC Business School

Although the entrepreneurial ecosystem (EE) has become a crucial concept for territorial economic development, digital transformation tends to reshape the architecture of EEs and reduce spatial dependencies. This constant evolution results in the regular emergence of new actors in the digital spectrum, and fundamentally modifies the design of EEs and their boundaries, which are no longer limited to a predefined set of actors concentrated on a given territory, but to a multi-dimensional approach: 1) entrepreneurial actors, 2) entrepreneurial organizations, and 3) institutions, which can coordinate formally and informally to help generate and improve entrepreneurial activity within a specific local environment.

Appel publié par Revue internationale P M E Économie et gestion de la petite et moyenne entreprise. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Digitization of entrepreneurial ecosystems (EEs): Impact of digital transformation on EEs, new relationships and governance possibilities within entrepreneurial ecosystems
  • Relationships between ecosystems: Infra/international cooperation and coopetition
  • Digital challenges for entrepreneurial ecosystem actors: incubators, accelerators, financial actors, SMEs, etc.
  • Consequences of digitization: dehumanization, environmental impact, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), inequalities (gender, emerging countries)
  • Behavior and strategy of stakeholders in Digital Entrepreneurial Ecosystems (DEEs): impacts on startups and SMEs
  • Relational approaches within DEEs: network structures between EEs and entrepreneurs, intra and inter DEEs
  • Inclusion and openness to social, territorial, gender and ethnocultural diversity through DEE development
  • Boundaries between EEs and DEEs for entrepreneurial stimulation
  • Conceptual proximity and diversity, overlaps between concepts? Substitution and/or complementarity?
  • Public policy issues, entrepreneurial processes and innovation practices in the context of DEEs
  • Economic models and digital transformation for SMEs and EEs
  • Interactions between digital platforms and EEs
  • Ecosystem for supporting entrepreneurs and SMEs in their digital transformation
  • Digital maturity of companies and entrepreneurial ecosystems in digital transformation
